member.name: T:KSP.Sim.impl.CollisionManager
member.summary:
Manage PhysX interactions to ignore collisions between colliders in the same vessel.
The primary mechanism for this is Physics.IgnoreCollision(). However, doing that for every collider combination scales O(n^2). Scalability problems become measurable around 100 parts, and can take several minutes after 900+ parts.
It is much faster to only set up ignores for parts that are actually touching. This scales close to O(n) with the collider count. However, it's difficult to test this in advance. So we just let PhysX tell us which are touching, because that's what it's designed to do.
- Record each collider as being "owned" by a vessel (guid) - Wait for PhysX to report a contact. - CollisionMonitor receives a Physics.ContactModifyEvent for the contact. (The callback is offthread) - If the contact is between to colliders owned by the same vessel GUID, void the contact. (This allows them to pass through as if already ignored) - Log the contact in a thread-safe structure. - At some later point on the main thread, read the log, set do the Physics.IgnoreCollision(), and (optionally) log again so that it can be undone.
There are some cases that require special handling:
- Collider setups that won't generate Physics.ContactModifyEvent() callbacks (usually because they are temporarily on the same Rigidbody), but need to be ignored anyway. It is necessary to call Physics.IgnoreCollision() in advance. ("always ignore") - Some ignores need to persist despite the collider being removed from the vessel. ("persist after removal"). This is usually a separable item (e.g., engine shroud) significantly overlaps other colliders (e.g., the engine it contains). If the ignore is removed too soon, the resulting contact event can lead to RUD.

member.name: M:KSP.Sim.impl.SwimKerbalCharacterStateHandler.ComputeSwimMoveDirection(UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Vector3,System.Single)
member.summary: Combines the camera relative swim input with the vertical dive input into a single world space swim direction. The horizontal part is flattened onto the horizon plane, exactly as surface swimming has always done, and the vertical part is applied along the horizon up axis. The result is normalized, so diving diagonally moves the kerbal at the same speed as swimming straight forward.
member.param: The horizontal swim input, already rotated into world space by the flight camera.
The world space horizon up axis at the kerbal's position.
The vertical input, positive to swim up and negative to swim down.
member.returns: A unit length world space swim direction, or when there is no usable input.

What a module releases here lives outside the part and outlives it: message-bus subscriptions, and resource-flow request entities registered against the vessel. member.remarks:
Captures a snapshot of property states before toggling, as symmetry propagation will update property states mid loop, leading to a 2 (or other even) item symmetry group scenario not seemingly toggling as it does this:
Initial state: 1: false 2: false
Iteration 1 -> Invert 1 1: invert -> true 2: symmetry propagates -> true
Iteration 2 -> Invert 2 1: symmetry propagates -> false 2: invert -> false
Final state: 1: false 2: false
So to counteract this bug, the initial state is snapshotted at the beginning, leading to a state like
Initial state: 1: false 2: false
Iteration 1 -> Invert 1 from initial 1: invert -> true 2: symmetry propagates -> true
Iteration 2 -> Invert 2 from initial 1: symmetry propagates -> true 2: invert -> true
Final state: 1: true 2: true

member.summary: Reconciles a stage situation list against the number of stages in the staging stack, padding with when short and trimming from the tail when long.
member.param: The stage situation list to reconcile.
The number of stages the list must describe.
The situation to add for stages that have no entry yet.
True while a craft is loading, which skips the reconciliation entirely.
Optional list that receives the trimmed entries, tail first.
member.returns: True when the list was modified, false when it already matched or was left alone.
member.remarks: Fixes #1000: the staging stack is rebuilt one stage at a time while a craft loads, so reconciling against its transient count trims the situations just restored from the craft file off the tail.

member.name: M:KSP.Sim.DeltaV.DeltaVExtensions.ClampSituationToBody(KSP.Sim.State.DeltaVSituation,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Coerces a situation into a combination the given body actually supports: airless bodies force vacuum at zero altitude, and altitudes are clamped to the body's atmosphere or terrain ceiling.
member.param: The situation to coerce.
The body's atmosphere depth in meters. Zero or less means airless.
The body's highest terrain in meters.
member.returns: The coerced situation.
member.remarks: Defensive (#1000): mirrors the clamping the delta-V tool applies when a body is picked, so a situation read from a craft file cannot feed the delta-V maths values the UI would never produce and then displays clamped, making the shown altitude disagree with the computed one.

member.name: M:KSP.Sim.DeltaV.DeltaVExtensions.SanitizeSituation(KSP.Sim.State.DeltaVSituation,KSP.Sim.State.DeltaVSituation)
member.summary: Validates a situation against the current universe, coercing it to what its body supports.
member.param: The situation to validate, typically read from a craft file.
The situation to return when the named body is not in the current universe.
member.returns: The coerced situation, or when the body is unknown.
member.remarks: Defensive (#1000): craft files can name bodies this install does not have, and can carry atmosphere/altitude combinations no longer valid for a body whose data changed.

member.summary: For a "facing-away" decoupler, marks all ancestors (the lower stages that get jettisoned) and their sibling subtrees as DecoupledMass at the decoupler's stage. member.name: T:KSP.Game.Load.ConsolidateSciencePointsSaveMigration014
member.summary: Save migration that consolidates the old multi-field science-point model into the single value introduced when science was moved from a derived player-level quantity to a stored agency-level balance.
member.remarks: The pre-consolidation available-science value was derived as SciencePointCapacity + AdditionalSciencePoints + (int)StartingScience - AllocatedSciencePoints. Capacity already had the ScienceRewards difficulty multiplier baked in when it was computed, so this migration uses the stored value verbatim and never re-applies any scaling. Unlocked tech nodes also moved from the player to the agency, so they are carried over here to avoid the R and D tree appearing empty on migrated saves.

member.summary: Starts fetching what the main menu shows, and lets the loading flow carry on without it.
member.remarks: The menu opens on the scene's own planet dressed as the body it means to show, so nothing it fetches has to be there before it can be seen. A published craft and a celestial body are a download and a bundle load, and waiting for them is the difference between a menu that opens and one that opens in ten seconds.

Unused, since nothing here failing should stop the game loading.

member.name: M:KSP.Game.Missions.SaveLoadMissionUtils.CollectConditionLatches(KSP.Game.Missions.Condition)
member.summary: Collects the latched progress of every condition in a tree, in the order a pre-order walk reaches them.
member.remarks: Only conditions reporting HasLatchedProgress take a slot, so a grouping condition such as contributes nothing of its own and appears only through its children. This records the few bits of state a condition tree accumulates rather than a copy of the tree, which keeps the definition authoritative when a mission is updated underneath a save.
member.param: The root of the condition tree to walk. May be null.
member.returns: One entry per latching condition, or an empty array when the tree is null or holds none.

member.name: M:KSP.Game.Missions.SaveLoadMissionUtils.TryApplyConditionLatches(KSP.Game.Missions.Condition,System.Boolean[])
member.summary: Restores previously collected latches onto a condition tree, matching them up by the same pre-order walk.
member.remarks: Refuses the whole array when its length does not match the tree, which is what happens when a mission definition gains or loses a condition while a save that predates the change is still around. Discarding is the safe outcome there, since applying positionally would silently attach one condition's progress to another.
member.param: The root of the condition tree to restore onto. May be null.
The array previously produced by . May be null.
member.returns: True if the latches were applied, false if they were refused and the tree left untouched.

member.name: M:KSP.Game.Missions.Definitions.MissionData.TryGetVesselRun(System.Int32,System.Int32@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Returns the bounds of the run of consecutive vessel-scoped stages that the given stage belongs to.
member.remarks: A run is every unbroken span of stages set to . One vessel has to carry a run from its first stage to its last, and a stage ends it, so the stages beyond are open to whichever vessel is flying by then. Runs are derived from the stage list rather than stored, so they cannot fall out of step with the definition.
member.param: The index of the stage to locate.
When this method returns true, the index of the run's first stage.
When this method returns true, the index of the run's last stage.
member.returns: True if the stage is vessel-scoped and therefore part of a run, false otherwise.

member.name: M:KSP.Game.CelestialBodyProvider.GetCenterVisibility(System.String,KSP.Sim.Position,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String})
member.summary: Added for issue #363. Returns a 0–1 visibility value indicating whether the center point of is occluded by any body in when viewed from . Unlike disc-area visibility, this uses the star's center point so that the lens flare — which renders as a screen-space overlay at the star's projected position — does not bleed through an occluder's disc. Returns 0 when the center is hidden, fading to 1 over half the target's angular radius as the center clears the occluder's edge.

member.name: M:KSP.Game.SaveLoadDialogFileEntry.BindListRow(KSP.Game.ExtendedSaveFileInfo,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,KSP.Game.CampaignLoadMenu)
member.summary: Fills this entry with a save for a recycled list row, without raising a selection.
member.remarks: selects the entry and reports it to the owning menu when it is the last played one, which is right for a list built once but wrong for a row that gets reused as the player scrolls. Selection is decided by the caller here and applied without notifying, so scrolling past the last played save cannot steal the player's choice.
member.param: The extended save file info to display.
True to show the most recently played tag on this row.
True when this row represents the currently selected save.
The campaign load menu that owns this entry.

members.member: <summary> Sorted array of all registered discovery names, populated during <see cref="Initialize" />. </summary>
<summary> Indicates whether <see cref="Initialize" /> has been called and the discovery cache is populated. </summary>
<summary> Gets the read-only bidirectional mapping between discovery names and their corresponding message types. </summary>

<summary> Scans all loaded assemblies for types decorated with <see cref="DiscoverableMessage" /> and populates the discovery name and type cache. Sorts all registered discovery names into <see cref="DiscoveryNamesSorted" />. Has no effect if already initialized. </summary>

<summary> Returns the message type registered under the given discovery name. </summary> <param name="discoveryName">The discovery name to look up.</param> <returns>The <see cref="System.Type" /> registered for <paramref name="discoveryName" />, or <c>null</c> if not found, the name is empty, or the registry is not initialized.</returns>

<summary> Returns the discovery name registered for the given message type. </summary> <param name="messageType">The message type to look up.</param> <returns>The discovery name string registered for <paramref name="messageType" />, or <c>null</c> if not found, the type is null, or the registry is not initialized.</returns>

<summary> Returns the discovery name registered for the message type <typeparamref name="T" />. </summary> <typeparam name="T">The message type whose discovery name is retrieved.</typeparam> <returns>The discovery name string registered for <typeparamref name="T" />, or <c>null</c> if not found or the registry is not initialized.</returns>

<summary> Returns the zero-based index of the given discovery name within the sorted <see cref="DiscoveryNamesSorted" /> array. </summary> <param name="discoveryName">The discovery name to locate.</param> <returns>The zero-based index of <paramref name="discoveryName" /> in <see cref="DiscoveryNamesSorted" />, or <c>-1</c> if not found or the registry is not initialized.</returns>

member.name: T:KSP.Modules.CrewSeatReconciler
member.summary: Works out which interior seats of a crewed part must be emptied and which must be filled for its seat models to hold exactly the Kerbals the roster places in that part.
member.remarks: Issue #1005: seat state used to be driven by the position index carried on a single location-change message. A move between two seats of the same part matched neither the departure nor the arrival branch, so the models kept the old seat while the roster moved on. Every later move then emptied the roster's index instead of the seat that actually held the Kerbal, stranding a live character model and showing the Kerbal twice. Reconciling against the roster rather than against a message index cannot drift that way.

member.name: M:KSP.Modules.CrewSeatReconciler.Reconcile(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.Nullable{KSP.Sim.impl.IGGuid}},System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.Nullable{KSP.Sim.impl.IGGuid}},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32})
member.summary: Collects the seat indices to empty and the seat indices to fill so the seats match the roster. A seat already holding the right Kerbal is reported in neither list, so its character model survives untouched. Seats whose occupant changes appear in both: the caller must empty every reported seat before filling any.
member.param: The Kerbal each seat model currently shows, where the seat shows nobody.
The Kerbal the roster places in each seat, where the roster seats nobody.
Receives the seat indices to empty, in ascending order. Cleared first.
Receives the seat indices to fill, in ascending order. Cleared first.

member.name: M:KSP.Modules.Module_CrewedInterior.CheckExternalSeatKerbalOverheat(System.Single)
member.summary: Tracks a virtual Kerbal temperature and removes Kerbals seated in an external seat when it exceeds . Fixes #600. The seat's own reentry flux is always zero because the occlusion algorithm sets ExposedAreaProportion=0 when the seat is behind the shock cone of a forward part. Instead, the Kerbal's heating is computed directly from vessel Mach number and air density - mirroring Module_Parachute - with ExposedAreaProportion=1.0 (the Kerbal is fully immersed in plasma even when the seat part itself is aerodynamically shielded) and the EVA Kerbal's body area (1.245 m2).

member.name: M:KSP.ScriptInterop.IScriptEnvironment.ForkIsolated(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Forks a child environment that shares this environment's VM but gets its own globals table chained to the parent's via an __index metatable. Reads of names absent on the child fall through to the parent. Writes land on the child, so per-environment globals stay isolated from the parent and from sibling forks.
member.param: The child environment's name.
Whether the child may run external interop.
member.returns: The isolated child environment.

member.name: M:KSP.Rendering.Planets.PQData.FaceRotation(UnityEngine.Vector3)
member.summary: Returns the rotation taking a root face's local frame onto the given outward face normal.
member.remarks:
Quaternion.FromToRotation leaves the rotation axis undefined when its arguments are antiparallel, so the engine picks one. The yNeg face normal is exactly (0, -1, 0) and is the only one of the six roots that hits that case. Unity 6.4 and earlier resolved it as 180 degrees about X, and Unity 6.5 resolves it as 180 degrees about Z, which yaws that face 180 degrees and points all four of its entries in the root adjacency table at the opposite face. Quads along the face seam then wait forever on a neighbour half a world away that never subdivides, so terrain in a band around the seam stalls at a coarse subdivision level and produces no colliders.
Pinning the antiparallel case keeps the frame the adjacency table in was authored against, rather than inheriting whichever axis the engine happens to choose.
member.param: The unit outward normal of the root face.
member.returns: The rotation from the local frame to the face's orientation.

member.param: The planet quad-sphere whose target position and body radius supply the distance calculation.

member.name: M:KSP.OAB.ObjectAssemblyBuilderFileIO.ApplyStageDeltaVSituations(System.Collections.Generic.List{KSP.Sim.State.StagePartsState},KSP.OAB.IObjectAssembly,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Writes the stage situations saved in a craft file onto an assembly, validating each one and leaving stages whose saved entry names no celestial body (craft files predating this data) on the builder default.
member.param: The saved stage records. Entry i holds the situation for vessel stage (count - i).
The assembly to write the situations onto.
True while parsing a craft, when the list must be rebuilt to the saved stage count. False once staging exists, when the assembly's own stage count is authoritative and only the values are refreshed.
member.remarks: The refresh call must run after staging has been rebuilt: the staging stack grows one stage at a time while a craft loads, and syncing the situation list against that transient count trims restored entries off its tail.

member.name: M:KSP.OAB.ObjectAssemblyBuilderFileIO.GetSavedStageSituation(System.Collections.Generic.List{KSP.Sim.State.DeltaVSituation},System.Int32,System.Int32,KSP.Sim.State.DeltaVSituation)
member.summary: Returns the delta-V situation a craft file's stage record must carry.
member.param: The assembly's stage situations.
The index of the stage record being written.
The number of stage records the file will hold.
The situation to write when the stage has none stored.
member.returns: The situation to store in the record.
member.remarks: Craft files hold the situations in reverse stage order, so reads record k back into stage (recordCount - k). Record k must therefore carry the situation of stage (recordCount - k) for a reload to put every setting back where the player left it. That is driven by the record count, deliberately not by the assembly's live situation count: a craft can hold more stages than the file records (a first-firing stage with no stageable parts is not saved), and keying off the live count there would shift every setting onto a neighbouring stage. Covered by StageDeltaVSituationTests.

member.summary: Copies the stage situations saved in a craft file into a stage situation list.
member.param: The saved stage records. Entry i holds the situation for vessel stage (count - i).
The stage situation list to write into.
The situation used to fill stages the file has no data for.
True to rebuild the list to the saved stage count, false to write values into the existing entries only.
Optional validation applied to each saved situation before it is stored. When null, values are stored as they were read.
member.remarks: Split out from so the craft-file ordering can be tested without an assembly or a running game.

member.name: F:KSP.IO.IOProvider._hijackableBaseTypes
member.summary: The base types no discovered converter may claim. A converter matching one of these matches almost everything, and it is consulted ahead of both the contract and the type discriminator.

member.name: M:KSP.IO.IOProvider.ClaimsHijackableBaseType(Newtonsoft.Json.JsonConverter)
member.summary: Reports whether a converter claims one of the base types in .
member.remarks: Converters are discovered by reflectively scanning every loaded assembly, so a package added to the project contributes its own whether or not it is meant for game data. Two have already caused bugs. One claiming UnityEngine.Object rewrote every ScriptableObject as a bare name and instance ID reference, which broke the camera tweakables (#1016). One claiming System.Object consumed every object-typed slot before the $type discriminator was read, so campaign plugin save data came back as a raw JObject and the copy into the real save data class threw, which broke the VAB on entry (#1024).
member.param: The converter to probe.
member.returns: True if the converter claims a base type it must not, otherwise false.

member.name: P:AwesomeTechnologies.VegetationSystem.VegetationSystemPro.PolarSphereToWorld
member.summary: Gets the matrix taking polar sphere local space to world space.
member.remarks: Cell bounding spheres are computed from lat and lon in the body's local frame, while spawned instances are in world space, so the conversion needs the body's full transform rather than just its position. Rotation is the part that matters in practice, because the planet authoring framing helpers rotate the PQS transform to bring a lat and lon into view. Falls back to identity so a system with no transform assigned behaves as it did when only the position was applied.

member.name: P:AwesomeTechnologies.VegetationSystem.VegetationSystemPro.PolarSphereRotation
member.summary: Gets the polar sphere's rotation alone, with no translation.
member.remarks: For the culling path only. BoundingSphereCullJob adds FloatingOriginOffset to every sphere before testing it and subtracts it afterwards, so culling volumes must be built body-centred and world-oriented. Handing that path a full local-to-world matrix applies the translation twice, which is invisible in an authoring scene where the body sits at the world origin and is a full body radius of error in flight.

member.name: M:AwesomeTechnologies.VegetationSystem.VegetationSystemPro.BootForEditor
member.summary: Initializes the vegetation system for both play mode and editor mode.
member.remarks: Play mode reaches this through OnEnable. Outside play mode nothing calls OnEnable, so the editor preview driver calls this directly once the PQS and the terrain bridge are ready. Every allocation the system owns is made here, so a system that has not been booted has InitDone false and no compute shaders, cell spawner or studio cameras.

member.name: M:AwesomeTechnologies.VegetationSystem.VegetationSystemPro.UpdateForEditor
member.summary: Performs the per-frame culling and cell spawning for both play mode and editor mode.
member.remarks: Play mode reaches this through Update. Edit mode has no Update, so the editor preview driver calls it directly, which is why the play mode check that used to guard the whole body has been removed. The camera auto-selection below stays play mode only, because the editor supplies its own SceneView camera rather than hunting for a gameplay one.

member.name: M:AwesomeTechnologies.VegetationSystem.VegetationSystemPro.DisposeAllVegetationCells
member.summary: Disposes all vegetation cells and clears pending spawn queues.

member.name: M:AwesomeTechnologies.VegetationSystem.VegetationSystemPro.LateUpdateForEditor
member.summary: Performs the per-frame indirect render for both play mode and editor mode.
member.remarks: Play mode reaches this through LateUpdate. The editor preview driver calls it from the SceneView camera callback so the queued draw is set and consumed in the same frame.

member.name: M:AwesomeTechnologies.VegetationSystem.VegetationSystemPro.ShutdownForEditor
member.summary: Releases everything allocated and clears the init flag.
member.remarks: Play mode reaches this through OnDisable. The editor preview driver calls it on session teardown, before the PQS is deactivated, because the scatter jobs read PQS-owned containers. Idempotent, since a session can end after a boot that failed part way.

member.name: M:AwesomeTechnologies.VegetationSystem.VegetationCell.GetPolarBoundingSphere(System.Single,UnityEngine.Matrix4x4)
member.summary: Returns a bounding sphere for this cell projected onto the polar sphere and transformed by .
member.remarks:
PolarToCartesian works in the polar sphere's local frame, so its result has to be taken through the body transform before being compared against anything in world space. The caller decides how much of that transform to supply, and the two cases are not interchangeable. Culling passes rotation only, because BoundingSphereCullJob adds FloatingOriginOffset itself and would otherwise translate twice. Callers that compare against a raw world camera position pass the full local-to-world matrix.
Only the cheap trigonometric part is cached, keyed on radius. The transform is applied on every call so that a rotating body does not invalidate the cache every frame, which would defeat the point of having one.
member.param: The radius of the planet sphere used for polar projection.
Rotation only for culling, or the full local-to-world matrix for world-space comparisons.
member.returns: A enclosing this cell as it appears on the curved planet surface.

member.name: T:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuHostPlanet
member.summary: Dresses the menu scene's own planet as Duna, for the menu to open on while a real body loads behind it.
member.remarks: This is paint rather than a celestial body: three textures, a retinted atmosphere, and the cloud layers taken off. It costs nothing to put up, which is the whole point of it. A real body is a bundle load of several seconds, and a menu that waits for one opens several seconds late.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuHostPlanet.Dress(UnityEngine.Transform)
member.summary: Paints the scene planet as Duna.
member.remarks: The atmosphere components bake how they look when they are enabled, so changing their colours while they are running changes nothing. They are stopped, told, and started again a frame later.
member.param: The scene planet.
member.returns: An enumerator that finishes once the atmosphere has been rebuilt in its new colours.

member.name: T:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuVesselLightRecord
member.summary: What a menu part's lights and lit surfaces are, kept so they can still be switched once the modules that described them are gone.
member.remarks: A menu craft has no vessel behind it, so the builder destroys every part module the moment it has read their state. That takes the authoring with it: which lights belong to a lamp, how bright each is meant to be, and which materials on a crew pod are its windows. This is written while the modules are still there and read long after they are not.

member.summary: Gets how far each light in reaches on the craft as it was authored.
member.remarks: Kept rather than left on the light because the menu draws a craft at whatever size frames it, and a light's reach is not a distance that scales with the thing it is attached to. A lamp authored to fill a cabin lights a fraction of one drawn several times life size.

member.name: T:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuSunLight
member.summary: The menu's sun: the light everything is lit by, and the flares that are the sun on screen.
member.remarks: Nothing in the game drives either of these in the menu. The lighting system that scales a star by distance gives up as soon as it sees the main menu, and no code anywhere writes a flare's brightness, so both are exactly what the scene was authored with. That makes the authored values the one arrangement known to look right, which is why they are captured and scaled from rather than replaced.

member.summary: How quickly the menu turns from one craft and body to the next.

member.name: T:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetTracker
member.summary: Holds which planet the main menu shows behind whatever vessel is on screen.
member.remarks: The vessel rotation and the planet are built by different things at different times and neither owns the other, so this sits between them the way the vessel credit does. An ask naming the planet already up raises nothing, since a channel publishing several vessels against one body names it for every one of them and restaging the planet between them is exactly what should not happen.

member.name: P:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetTracker.Current
member.summary: Gets the body currently shown, which is nothing until something names one.
member.remarks: Deliberately not the default body to start with. Nothing the menu shows may load before Patch Manager has run, and a planet that was already named would be loaded by the loader the moment it existed, which is well before that. Starting at nothing means the first ask is always a change, whatever it names.

member.name: E:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetTracker.Changed
member.summary: Raised when the planet changes, and only then.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetTracker.Show(System.String)
member.summary: Names the body that should be shown behind whatever has just come on screen.
member.param: The body named by the entry that published the vessel, which may be null, blank or oddly cased. Naming nothing means the default body, which is what one of the rotation's own prefabs shows against.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetTracker.Clear
member.summary: Forgets the body being shown, for when the menu is left and the next visit should start from nothing rather than from whatever the last vessel of this one happened to name.
member.remarks: Raises nothing. There is no menu left to tell, and the next visit names its own body once its content has loaded.

member.name: P:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuVesselRotationSession.CurrentAsyncLoadHandle
member.summary: The handle callers gate a scene transition on, which is valid at all times and done whenever no addressable load is outstanding.
member.remarks: Before OTA content this rotation only ever loaded addressables, so a load being in flight and the handle being valid were the same thing, and consumers wait on exactly that. A workspace vessel is built rather than loaded and has no addressable operation behind it, so reporting nothing would leave those consumers waiting on a handle that only turns valid again when the rotation happens to land on a stock vessel, or never at all while the pool holds workspaces alone. The idle handle answers that honestly: there is nothing addressable left to wait for.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuVesselRotationSession.TravelOffset(UnityEngine.Transform,System.Single)
member.summary: Works out how far a craft travels on its way out, and along which way.
member.remarks:
KSP parts stack on their local Y, so a craft's nose is its root's up rather than any Unity forward. The distance is measured against the craft itself, so a large one travels further and both leave frame. A craft leaves along this and the next one arrives from the other end of it, which is what makes an arrival read as a different craft rather than the same one coming back.
The two ends are not the same length. Leaving has only to end with the craft gone, while arriving has to look flown in from somewhere, so it is given the further distance to cover.
member.param: The craft.
How far to travel, as a multiple of the craft's own longest side.
member.returns: The offset from where it rests to where it is gone, in its parent's space.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuVesselRotationSession.IsMenuRevealed
member.summary: Whether the menu is actually in front of somebody rather than still behind the loading curtain.
member.remarks:
Asked of the curtain itself, and of both of its answers. It stops calling itself shown the moment it begins to fade, which is half a second before anything can be seen through it, and the loading flow finishes earlier still. Either of those on its own opens the gate while the picture is a fade away.
The photosensitivity warning stands in front of the menu after the curtain has gone, and a craft changing behind it spends its whole time on screen unseen. The legal flow raises its own gate for as long as it is up, including not at all when there is nothing to accept.
member.returns: True once the curtain is gone and nothing stands in front of the menu.

That is exactly wrong for a craft the turn is meant to be getting rid of: it rides along, stays in frame the whole way round, and there is never a moment it can be taken away unseen. Left where they stand in the world instead, they sweep out of frame like the planet does.

member.name: T:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath
member.summary: Everything the main menu works out for itself: which body a channel named, where a planet and a craft belong on screen, and the shapes they move along between one arrangement and the next.
member.remarks: The menu shows bodies and craft at whatever size and place suit the picture rather than at any scale the game already has an answer for, so all of this is its own problem. It lives together because it is the whole of what can be worked out without a scene to look at, which is also the whole of what can be tested without running the game.

member.name: F:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.DEFAULT_BODY
member.summary: The body shown when a manifest names none, which is what the menu showed before it could be chosen.

member.name: F:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.PERCEIVED_BRIGHTNESS_EXPONENT
member.summary: How much of a change in light an eye actually sees. Perceived brightness goes roughly as intensity to this power, which is why a room lit at half the wattage does not look half as bright.

member.name: F:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.VESSEL_LIGHT_SUN_SCALE
member.summary: How dim the sun has to get before a craft turns its own lights on. Half the light the menu was built around, which falls between Duna and Dres with neither of them anywhere near it.

member.name: F:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.MAX_ORBIT_CHAIN_STEPS
member.summary: How far up a chain of what orbits what to follow before giving up. A definition that names a body as orbiting itself, directly or round a longer loop, would otherwise be followed forever.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.ResolveBodyAddress(System.String)
member.summary: Returns the addressable key for a body's scaled space prefab.
member.remarks: No list of bodies is checked against. A name this does not recognise fails to load and falls back on its own, and hard coding the roster would stop a body added later from ever being publishable.
member.param: The body named by the manifest, which may be null, blank or oddly cased.
member.returns: The addressable key, falling back to the default body when no usable name was given.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.ResolveBodyName(System.String)
member.summary: Returns the body name that will actually be used, after trimming, casing and the fallback.
member.remarks: A name that is already mixed case is taken verbatim, since bodies like AsteroidA01 carry capitals a naive rule would flatten. Only an all lowercase name has its first letter raised, so that the common case of writing "eve" in a hand written manifest resolves.
member.param: The body named by the manifest, which may be null, blank or oddly cased.
member.returns: The resolved body name.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.TryResolveBodyChange(System.String,System.String,System.String@)
member.summary: Works out whether a named body is a change from the body already up.
member.remarks: A channel publishing several vessels against one body names that body for every one of them, so most asks are for the planet already showing. Settling it before anything downstream is told is what keeps an ask that changes nothing from costing a planet load.
member.param: The body already up, resolved, or null when there is none.
The body named by whatever is on screen, which may be null, blank or oddly cased.
Receives the body asked for, resolved, whether or not it is a change.
member.returns: True if the body asked for is a different one, false if it is the body already up.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.SolveParkPosition(UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Vector3)
member.summary: Solves where a planet waits while it is loaded but not being shown.
member.remarks: The camera turns the whole way round during a change, so there is no direction it does not sweep past except one: the axis it turns about. A body put on that axis stays square to the view at every angle the camera reaches, which is the only place it can wait without being seen. It is held at the distance it will be shown at, so it is never drawn at a size it should not be if a frame catches it on its way in.
member.param: Where the planet rests when it is the one being shown.
The camera it waits beside.
The axis the camera turns about, which is the camera's own up.
member.returns: Where the planet waits.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.TrySolveScaleFactor(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single@)
member.summary: Solves the scale factor for a body of a known real size drawn at a known size on screen.
member.remarks: The atmosphere shader works in kilometres against a sphere it assumes is the body's real size, so it has to be told how many of those kilometres one scene unit stands for. Flight hard codes the figure because every flight scene is at the same scale, and map view derives it from the map camera, which the menu does not have.
member.param: The body's real radius in kilometres, which is the atmosphere model's bottom radius.
The radius the body's mesh actually occupies, in scene units.
Receives the metres of real body one scene unit stands for.
member.returns: True if both sizes were usable, false if either was zero or negative, which is a body measured before its mesh existed.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.TrySolveFraming(UnityEngine.Vector3,System.Single,UnityEngine.Vector3,System.Single,System.Single,UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Vector3@,UnityEngine.Vector3@)
member.summary: Solves for the local position and scale that put a vessel's bounds centre on the anchor at the target size.
member.remarks: A workspace lays its parts out around whichever part is the root, so a craft's origin is wherever the builder happened to start rather than the middle of it, and a craft is whatever size its author made it. The scale multiplies whatever the vessel is already at, since the extent being corrected was measured at that scale.
member.param: Centre of the assembled bounds, in the parent's space.
Longest side of the assembled bounds, at the current scale.
Where in the parent's space the craft's centre should end up.
Smallest longest side a craft may end up occupying.
Largest longest side a craft may end up occupying.
The vessel root's local position, which the bounds were measured at.
The vessel root's local scale, which the bounds were measured at.
The solved local position.
The solved local scale.
member.returns: True if the craft could be framed, false if it measured nothing usable, in which case the caller leaves it where the build put it rather than scaling it by infinity.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.SolveBodyFramingScale(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Solves how much to shrink a body so its terrain does not crowd the craft in front of it.
member.remarks: Every body's surface sits at the same distance from its own centre in the mesh it is drawn from, so two bodies drawn side by side fill the frame the same way however large either of them really is. What breaks that is terrain: a mountain is a rounding error against a planet's radius and most of the body on a rock a mile across, and it is the drawn shape rather than the sphere under it that runs into the craft. Pulling the body back by exactly what it overhangs leaves a smooth one untouched and gives a lumpy one the same room in frame.
member.param: How far the drawn body reaches from its centre, where it faces the craft.
How far the surface would reach with no terrain on it.
member.returns: What to multiply the body's scale by, which is one for a body that does not overhang its own sphere.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.ShouldLightVessel(System.Single)
member.summary: Works out whether a craft should have its own lights on for the body it is being shown against.
member.remarks: A craft at Jool or Eeloo is lit by a fifth of the sun Kerbin gets, and a menu is meant to show it off rather than to be accurate about how little of it can be made out. The threshold sits where nothing in the stock system is near it: Dres is the dimmest body above the line by a comfortable margin and Duna the brightest below, so no body is one rounding away from flipping.
member.param: How bright the sun is for that body, against the body the menu was lit for.
member.returns: True if the craft should light itself.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.ExcludingPrevious``1(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{``0},``0)
member.summary: Narrows what the rotation may pick next so it does not pick what is already on screen.
member.remarks: The rotation takes each thing it shows out of the pool and refills the pool once it empties, so it works through everything before repeating. The one place it can repeat is across that refill, where what just went back in the pool is what is still on screen, and with two things published that is every other change.
member.typeparam: What is being picked between.
member.param: Everything that could be picked.
What was picked last, which may be nothing.
member.returns: The candidates worth picking between, which is all of them when the one already up is the only thing there is to show.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.TrySolveStarOrbitRadius(KSP.Sim.SerializedGalaxyDefinition,System.String,System.Double@)
member.summary: Works out how far a body orbits from its star, following whatever it orbits until something orbits the star itself.
member.remarks: A moon is lit by however far its planet is from the star, not by how far it is from its planet, and a body's own prefab knows nothing about what it orbits. The galaxy definition is where that is written down, and it is the same definition Patch Manager edits, so a body moved by a patch and a body added by one both answer here.
member.param: The galaxy definition, which may be null if none has loaded.
The body to measure, which is its identifier in the definition.
Receives the semi major axis of the orbit that goes around the star.
member.returns: True if a distance was found, false for a star, a body the definition does not name, or a chain that leads nowhere.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.SolveSunScale(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Solves how much brighter or dimmer the sun is at one distance than at another.
member.remarks: Light falls off with the square of distance, which is true and unusable on its own: it puts the outer planets at a few percent of the light the menu was lit and framed against, and the inner ones far past the top of the range. An eye does not work that way. Brightness is perceived closer to the fifth root of the square of intensity, so the physical figure is passed through that same response and what comes out is a picture that reads as further from the sun rather than one that reads as unlit.
member.param: The distance the menu's own lighting was set up at.
The distance of the body being shown.
member.returns: What to multiply the menu's authored sun by, or one when either distance is missing, which leaves the sun exactly as it was authored.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuMath.ResolveParentName(KSP.Sim.SerializedCelestialBody)
member.summary: Returns what a body orbits, which the definition writes down in two places.
member.remarks: A body carries a reference of its own and its orbit carries one too. They agree in everything shipped, but only one of them has to be filled in for the definition to load, so both are read.
member.param: The body to look at.
member.returns: What it orbits, or null when it orbits nothing, which is what a star does.

member.name: T:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuRotationTuning
member.summary: How long a craft takes to leave and to arrive, and a way to watch it happen on demand.
member.remarks:
These are settled by eye rather than by argument, and the only way to judge a value is to see a craft move at it. Waiting out the half minute a craft stays up between changes, restarting the game to try the next number, is most of the cost of picking one, so the numbers are reachable while the menu is up and a change can be asked for at any moment:
Ksp2Redux.Cli.exe eval csharp "Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuRotationTuning.RotateNow(3f, 1.5f)"
What is set here stays set until or the game is restarted, so the same timing can be watched several times over. The length of the planet turn is not here: it belongs to a setting players can reach, and is read from that setting every time a turn begins.

member.name: F:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuRotationTuning.DEFAULT_LEAVE_SECONDS
member.summary: Seconds a craft takes to leave, as shipped.

member.summary: Seconds a craft takes to arrive, as shipped.

member.name: F:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuRotationTuning.DEFAULT_PLUME_SPOOL_SECONDS
member.summary: Seconds an engine takes to come up to full thrust, as shipped.

member.name: F:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuRotationTuning.DEFAULT_LEAVE_EXTENTS
member.summary: How far a craft goes on its way out, as a multiple of its own longest side.
member.remarks: Far shorter than the distance one arrives over. A departure only has to end with the craft off the screen, and anything past that point is spent watching an empty one.

member.name: F:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuRotationTuning.DEFAULT_ARRIVE_EXTENTS
member.summary: How far out a craft waits before it flies in, as a multiple of its own longest side.
member.remarks: Longer than the distance one leaves over, and not for symmetry: a craft has to come in fast enough to read as having flown from somewhere, and the distance is what it has to cover to earn that.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuWorkspaceVesselBuilder.TryMeasureVessel(UnityEngine.Transform,UnityEngine.Vector3@,System.Single@)
member.summary: Measures how much room a built vessel needs over a whole turn of its own spin.
member.remarks:
A craft on the menu turns constantly, so what it needs is the cylinder it sweeps rather than the box it fills at any one moment. Measuring the box instead ties the answer to whatever angle the craft happened to be at, so the same craft frames differently between showings, and a long one measured nose on is framed small and then overruns the frame as it comes broadside.
Only what is drawn counts. A particle renderer's bounds cover wherever its particles have reached rather than the craft, and an engine carries disabled exhaust plume meshes that are ordinary mesh renderers many times longer than the craft itself. Passing false to GetComponentsInChildren skips inactive objects but not disabled renderers on active ones, so the plumes have to be excluded on their own account.
member.param: The vessel root, which is also what the craft turns about.
Receives the middle of the swept cylinder, in the parent's space. It sits on the craft's own turning axis, so it stays put as the craft turns.
Receives the largest room the craft needs at any point in its turn.
member.returns: when the vessel had something to measure, and when it had no mesh renderers at all.

member.summary: Measures a craft across the renderers of a given kind.
member.param: The craft.
Whether skinned meshes count towards the measurement.
Receives the centre of what was measured, in the parent's space.
Receives the longest side of what was measured.
member.returns: True if anything was measured.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuWorkspaceVesselBuilder.SolveWidestAcrossSpin(UnityEngine.Transform,System.Collections.Generic.List{UnityEngine.Vector3})
member.summary: Returns the widest a craft ever gets across the screen, over its whole turn.
member.remarks: A craft turns about its own length while it is being shown, so how much of the picture it takes up left to right changes the whole time. The craft is turned right through and the widest reading kept, which is the one that has to fit. Its actual shape is turned rather than a cylinder drawn around it, because a rocket is nowhere near as wide as the cylinder its fins sweep out and sizing it as though it were leaves it a quarter smaller than asked for.
member.param: The craft.
Every corner of every measured renderer, in the craft's own space.
member.returns: The widest extent across the screen, in the parent's units.

member.name: T:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuCameraTurn
member.summary: Tracks how far the menu's camera has turned while the planet behind it is being changed.
member.remarks: A change of planet is a turn rather than a fade, because a celestial body cannot be part drawn: its atmosphere shell is drawn or it is not, with nothing in between. Turning the camera rather than the bodies is what keeps the sun, the starfield and the planet moving together, since all three are only ever what the camera happens to be pointing at. It goes the whole way round rather than stopping halfway, so it finishes facing exactly what it faced to begin with and nothing in the scene has to be carried anywhere.

member.summary: Turns the camera the whole way round, exchanging the planet behind it for the one that has been made ready as it passes the half turn. Does nothing when nothing is waiting.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetLoader.BindClouds(Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetInstance,System.Int32)
member.summary: Registers a planet's clouds and waits for their layers to arrive.
member.remarks: Registered as flight rather than as map, which is the opposite way round from the atmosphere. The map path reads the map camera every frame and the menu has none, so it throws on the frame after it is registered. The flight path reads no camera at all.
member.param: The planet whose clouds to register.
The load this belongs to, so a superseded one can give up.
member.returns: An enumerator that finishes once the clouds are up or have failed to arrive.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetLoader.DriveCloudLighting
member.summary: Writes over what the cloud components get wrong outside flight, once a frame, after they have run.
member.remarks: At the end of the frame rather than in a late update, because which of two late updates runs first is not something either of them decides. The components copy these values to their layers on the following frame, so writing here is what puts them in front of the copy rather than behind it.
member.returns: An enumerator that runs for as long as the menu is up.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetLoader.ShowPrepared
member.summary: Moves the planet that has been made ready into the place a planet is shown from, and destroys the one it replaces.
member.remarks: The one being replaced is not carried anywhere. Either the camera is facing away from where both of them are, which is the only point in a turn this is called from, or there was nothing to replace.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetLoader.ParkPlanet(Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetInstance)
member.summary: Puts a planet where it waits until it is the one being shown.
member.param: The planet to park, which may be nothing when none is waiting.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetLoader.AimCameras(System.Single)
member.summary: Aims every camera a change of planet turns at a given point in the turn.
member.remarks: Each camera yaws about its own up rather than all of them about one axis in the world. They do not share a frame to have a common axis in: the one drawing the starfield points a hundred and twenty degrees away from the one drawing the planets, and draws no scene at all, only its own skybox material. A single world axis is a yaw for one of them and mostly a roll for the other, which sends the stars across the picture at an angle to everything else in it.
member.param: How far round from where the cameras rest.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetLoader.ResolveTurningCameras
member.summary: Finds the cameras a change of planet turns, and records where each of them faces at rest.
member.remarks: Every camera under the rig turns, rather than a list of them by name, because whichever camera draws the starfield has to go round with whichever camera draws the planets or the two come apart. The rig's own camera is left out: it draws nothing, and the sun and the planets are its children, so turning it would take the picture and everything in it round together.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetLoader.ResolvePlanetCamera
member.summary: Finds the camera that actually draws the planets, which is not the one the menu is composed against.
member.remarks: Scaled space is rendered by a camera of its own, sitting nowhere near the flow camera the rest of the menu is framed by, and turning a planet about the wrong one sends it somewhere unrelated to the picture. Found by which camera's culling mask covers the layer the planet was put on.
member.returns: The camera, or null when nothing in the scene draws that layer.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetLoader.LoadGalaxyDefinition
member.summary: Reads the galaxy definition, once, and does nothing on every call after the first.
member.remarks: This runs after Patch Manager, because everything the menu loads does, so the definition read here is the patched one. It is the whole system rather than one body, so it is worth holding on to.
member.returns: An enumerator that finishes once the definition has loaded or failed to.

member.summary: Works out how bright the menu's sun should be for a body, from how far it orbits from its star.
member.param: The body's own data, which names it. May be null on a prefab without it.
member.returns: What to multiply the menu's authored sun by, or one when the distance is not known.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetLoader.FrameBody(UnityEngine.Transform,UnityEngine.MeshRenderer)
member.summary: Pulls a body in by however far its terrain overhangs the sphere underneath it.
member.remarks: Measured off the mesh rather than off the body as it stands, because the body turns and a box drawn around a turning shape changes size as it goes. Measured across the body rather than along its axis, because the craft sits over the equator and a peak at the pole never comes near it.
member.param: The planet to frame.
The renderer drawing the body.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetLoader.SolveScaleFactor(KSP.CoreCelestialBodyData,UnityEngine.Transform)
member.summary: Works out how many metres of real body one scene unit of a planet stands for.
member.remarks: Taken from the size the body is drawn at rather than measured off it, so terrain does not count towards a figure that is about the sphere. A body whose mountains are a real fraction of its radius would otherwise report itself far larger than it is, and be given an atmosphere to match.
member.param: The body's own data, which carries its real radius.
The planet, already framed, which is how big it is on screen.
member.returns: The scale factor, or zero when the body has nothing to measure.

member.summary: Binds the atmosphere model to the shell materials and tells them how big this planet is and where its light comes from.
member.remarks: This is the half of the component's own update that the menu can run. The other half reads the map camera every frame, which the menu does not have, so the component is stopped and this is called in its place. Both values it needs are fixed for as long as the planet is up.

member.name: M:Redux.UI.MainMenu.MainMenuPlanetInstance.SetCloudLighting(UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Color,System.Single)
member.summary: Tells this planet's clouds how big it is and what is lighting it.
member.remarks: Unlike the atmosphere, the cloud component is left running: it turns each layer against the wind, sizes them, orders them and binds their probes every frame, which is far more than is worth reproducing. Only what it gets wrong outside flight is written over. It assumes flight's fixed scaled space and a star light the menu does not have, so it would draw the clouds at the wrong size, lit white from straight up. This has to be called after the component's own update rather than before, or the frame's copy to the layers carries its values rather than these.
member.param: The direction light arrives from.
The colour of that light.
How strong that light is.

member.summary: Draws the purple dashed line from the active vessel to its main body's center in Map View while the Resource Gathering window is open, using Hslr instead of Shapes (Issue #985).
Controller for the MyFirstWindow UI.

Shows a small label at the point where the resource gathering line crosses the celestial body's surface, tracking that point on screen every frame the same way Map View's orbital markers (e.g. AN/DN, Ap/Pe) track their anchor position (Issue #985).

Populates the Resource Gathering window's "AVAILABLE RESOURCES AT {coordinates}" header with the active vessel's current surface coordinates, tinting the coordinates with the resource-gathering line color while the rest of the label keeps its stylesheet color (Issue #985).

member.name: M:Redux.UI.Flight.ResourceScannerWindowController.TryGetLineSurfaceCrossing(UnityEngine.Vector3,UnityEngine.Transform,UnityEngine.Vector3@)
member.summary: Finds where the vessel-to-body line crosses the body's surface. The radius is derived from the body's real physical radius and the vessel's real altitude (not the rendered mesh bounds) - Map View exaggerates celestial body mesh size for visibility/clickability at a distance, so a radius read from the mesh can exceed the real vessel-to-body distance and overshoot past the vessel entirely. Using the real radius/altitude ratio against the map-space distance guarantees the point always lands strictly between the body and the vessel.

member.name: T:Redux.Ecs.Systems.SimObjectDestroyEcbSystem
member.summary: Plays back the deferred destruction of simulation-object and transform entities once per frame, at the end of - after both (FixedUpdate) and (Update). Managed teardown still runs synchronously inside . Only the entity destruction waits, so no structural change lands in the middle of a reentrant destroy. Playback cascades each entity's and disposes its managed components, which is where every ObjectComponent.OnDispose runs.

member.name: F:Redux.Ecs.Systems.SimObjectDestroyEcbSystem.MAX_DRAIN_PASSES
member.summary: Upper bound on drain passes per frame. A managed OnDispose can destroy further objects, and each pass plays what the previous one recorded, so a cascade normally settles in two or three.

member.name: M:Redux.Ecs.Systems.SimObjectDestroyEcbSystem.ScheduleDestroy(Unity.Entities.Entity)
member.summary: Records the destruction of for end-of-frame playback. Destroys it immediately when there is no world or no system instance to defer through - editor tests and world teardown, where deferral has nothing to defer to.

member.name: M:Redux.Ecs.Systems.SimObjectDestroyEcbSystem.Flush
member.summary: Plays back everything recorded so far, synchronously. For callers that must not leave entities pending past their own teardown, such as .

member.name: M:Redux.Ecs.Systems.SimObjectDestroyEcbSystem.OnDestroy
member.summary: Discards pending commands without playing them back: the world is being torn down, so its entities are going away regardless.

member.name: M:Redux.Ecs.Systems.SimObjectDestroyEcbSystem.DetachGroupFromTransformGraph(Unity.Entities.Entity)
member.summary: Unlinks the entity and everything it owns from the transform graph while they all still exist. Playback destroys the whole at once, and an owned frame's managed Dispose runs as part of that destroy - too late to remove itself from its parent's child list, which would leave the parent holding a dead entry forever.

member.name: T:Redux.Ecs.Components.PatchedConicsOrbitData
member.summary: Unmanaged Keplerian state for a patched-conics orbit: the orbital elements plus the values derived from them during propagation. holds one of these and forwards its public API to it. The Keplerian math is (being) moved onto this struct as instance methods so it can later run in a Burst job.
member.remarks: All fields are blittable value types (the same ones already used inside Burst code such as Transformd and the n-body OdeSolveJob). Managed/coordinate-system-bound state (reference body, Vector velocity, patch graph, delegates) stays on the wrapper. The external Z-up frame is threaded into the math as a parameter.

member.name: T:Redux.Ecs.CompilerServices.ScanChangedModulesJob`2
member.summary: Walks through every entity of type , records the ones that have had a tracked value changed (with a snapshot of their changeset) to a queue, and clears the live changeset of each immediately.
member.remarks: Clearing here - rather than in a trailing reset pass - is what lets a write made from inside a notify callback (e.g. a symmetry copy) survive: its freshly set changeset bit is no longer wiped at the end of the same tick, so the following scan observes and notifies it.

member.name: T:Redux.CliIntegration.CliIntegrationServer
member.summary: Part-level methods: list parts with their PAW actions, invoke an action by name, typed verbs (deploy/converter/drill/crossfeed/decouple/undock), and part-to-part resource transfer via the resource flow request brokers.
Perf counter methods: per-tick ProfilerMarker capture, ECS chunk memory summary, and a curated list of marker names worth capturing.
Playtest run lifecycle: begin/assert/end/abort/report plus a fail-fast log matcher and a stall/deadline watchdog that finalize the run report on trip.
Localhost-only JSON-RPC server for CLI-driven editor integration.
Cheat methods: toggle infinite fuel/power difficulty options and quit the active session back to the main menu.

Scenario library: lists the repo's PlaytestScenarios manifest and loads a named scenario save, completing only after the sim is back in FlightView and the active vessel's situation has been stable for a settle window.
Clock control methods: read the sim clock, deterministically step the sim fixed group while paused, and run until a per-tick condition matches.
Event tap methods: capture published MessageCenter messages into a bounded in-memory buffer for later draining over the CLI.

member.name: T:Redux.Missions.VesselMissionRuntime
member.summary: Drives per-vessel mission progress from the running game.

member.name: M:Redux.Missions.VesselMissionRuntime.Tick(KSP.Game.GameInstance,KSP.Game.Missions.Definitions.MissionData)
member.summary: Advances a mission by one tick, keeping the active vessel's progress in step with it.
member.remarks: Replaces a bare call to . A mission on a vessel scoped stage does not tick at all while no vessel is active, so progress made at the space centre cannot be credited to nobody, and its progress is written back to the active vessel after every tick so switching craft needs no separate capture. A tick that carries the mission out of its run collapses the run instead.
member.param: The running game.
The mission to advance.

member.name: M:Redux.Missions.VesselMissionRuntime.OnActiveVesselChanged(KSP.Game.GameInstance)

member.name: M:Redux.Missions.VesselMissionRuntime.ReconcileOnLoad(KSP.Game.GameInstance)
member.summary: Settles per-vessel progress once a campaign has finished loading.
member.remarks: Two jobs. Progress that no longer describes anything is dropped: a save taken before a mission was finished leaves records on craft still in flight, and they would resurface as progress on something already sitting in the completed list, and the same sweep covers records for missions that no longer exist, which is what a definition withdrawn from downloaded content leaves behind. What survives is then handed to the mission for whichever craft the player is about to fly.
member.param: The running game.

member.name: M:Redux.Missions.VesselMissionRuntime.GetFleetCompletedStageIds(KSP.Game.GameInstance,KSP.Game.Missions.Definitions.MissionData)
member.summary: Returns the stages the fleet has finished on a mission's current run.
member.remarks: For Mission Control, which shows how far the fleet has got. The live mission holds whichever craft is flying, so reading it there would report an arbitrary one of several craft working the same run. This answers the question rather than writing the answer onto the mission everything else evaluates from.
member.param: The running game.
The mission being shown.
member.returns: The stage identifiers the furthest along craft has finished, or null when none has any.

member.name: T:Redux.Missions.VesselMissionProgressTransfer
member.summary: The rules for moving per-vessel mission progress between vessels, and for deciding which vessels may hold it.
member.remarks: Mirrors how science moves: joining two vessels merges their progress, splitting one gives both halves a copy, and nothing is ever partitioned or lost. Kept apart from the component so the rules can be tested without a simulation to hang them on.

member.name: M:Redux.Missions.VesselMissionProgressTransfer.Merge(Redux.Missions.VesselMissionRecord,Redux.Missions.VesselMissionRecord)
member.summary: Combines two vessels' progress on the same mission into the progress the joined vessel carries.
member.remarks: The record that reached the later stage wins, and its variables and latches come with it, since they describe the stage it is on rather than the one the other vessel is on. Completed stages are unioned, because a stage either vessel finished is finished for the craft they became.
member.param: One vessel's record. May be null.
The other vessel's record. May be null.
member.returns: The merged record, or null when neither side holds one.

member.summary: Merges every record held by one vessel into another.

member.summary: Gives one vessel a copy of everything another holds.
member.remarks: Used where a vessel is derived from another rather than joined to it: undocking, decoupling, and going out on EVA. Both sides keep their own copy and advance separately from that point.

The vessel being copied from. May be null.

member.name: M:Redux.Missions.VesselMissionProgressTransfer.InheritCreationStamp(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Returns the creation stamp a vessel joined from two others should carry.
member.remarks: Joining mints a new vessel, so the stamp has to be inherited rather than taken from the clock, or docking anything to an old station would present the station as newly built. The later of the two is taken, which matches the permissive rule the rest of these transfers use.
member.param: One vessel's creation stamp.
The other vessel's creation stamp.
member.returns: The stamp for the joined vessel.

member.name: M:Redux.Missions.VesselMissionProgressTransfer.IsVesselEligible(System.Double,System.Double,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns whether a vessel may work on a mission at all.
member.remarks: Every vessel qualifies unless the mission asks otherwise, which is how KSP1 contracts treat craft that already exist. When it does ask, a vessel qualifies only if it was built after the mission was picked up. That comparison is strictly later on purpose: a save written before either stamp existed has both at zero, and reading equal as eligible would waive the requirement on every campaign that predates this.
member.param: The universe time the vessel was created.
The universe time the mission was picked up.
Whether the mission asks for a craft built after it was picked up.
member.returns: True if the vessel may hold progress for the mission, false otherwise.

member.name: T:Redux.Lua.WaitLibrary
member.summary: Backs the Lua Wait global with the small set of C# leaf checks its yield loops poll each frame.
member.remarks: The Wait surface itself is defined in Lua (see ) because MoonSharp cannot yield a host coroutine from inside a CLR call - the loops must run on the Lua side, calling these leaves. Blocking forms (for example Wait.Seconds(2)) yield the calling coroutine until satisfied, so they only work inside a coroutine context (a console body, or a Game.StartCoroutine body). The callback forms (for example Wait.Seconds(2, fn)) are sugar that wraps the blocking form in Game.StartCoroutine, so they also work from a synchronous mod body. "Stop" is the runner ceasing to resume the coroutine, so the loops need no explicit cancel check. Stateless, one shared instance per env.

member.name: M:Redux.OTA.OTAContentService.RunThenResolve(System.Collections.IEnumerator,System.Action,System.String)
member.summary: Runs a routine to completion and resolves the loading flow afterwards, whether or not it got there.
member.param: The routine to run, which may be null.
The flow callback, called exactly once.
Names the routine in the log if it throws.
member.returns: A coroutine that always reaches its resolve.
member.remarks: An exception thrown inside a Unity coroutine ends it where it stands, so a routine that resolves on its last line never gets there and the flow action waits for a callback that is not coming. That is a hang on the loading screen rather than a caught error, and OTA content is not worth one. The routine is stepped by hand because C# will not allow a yield inside a try that has a catch.

member.name: T:Redux.OTA.OTAContentRepository
member.summary: Resolves a channel's files from the remote repository and the on-disk cache. Each file is validated against the manifest's SHA-256 before use. The cache is the source of truth when remote downloads are unavailable. This is the only class that touches the network or disk.

member.name: F:Redux.OTA.OTAContentRepository.DefaultRepositoryRootUrl
member.summary: Where content is served from unless an override points somewhere else.

member.name: F:Redux.OTA.OTAContentRepository.DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
member.summary: Seconds a single manifest or content download may take. Without one, an unresponsive host holds the loading curtain up for as long as the platform's own timeout allows, which is effectively forever. Generous enough for a large file on a slow connection, because the counts below are what actually bound the wait when a host is unreachable rather than merely slow.

member.name: F:Redux.OTA.OTAContentRepository.MAX_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS
member.summary: How many file downloads a channel keeps in flight at once. These files are small and the wait is almost all round-trip latency, so fetching them one at a time spends that latency once per file. The cap bounds how much is held in memory at a time and keeps the request rate reasonable for the host serving them.

member.name: T:Redux.Modules.Attributes.TransformNameAttribute
member.summary: Marks a string field as the bare leaf name of a single Transform within the part hierarchy. The runtime resolves the stored value to one specific Transform via recursive name search (FindChildRecursive / FindModelTransform / equivalent).
member.remarks:
Storage is just gameObject.name - never a slash-separated path. The author drags a Transform from the prefab and the leaf name is written automatically.
Use this attribute when the field references one specific Transform by name. For fields whose name groups multiple transforms (engine thrust transforms, gimbal targets, etc.), use . For fields resolved via transform.Find(path) with slash-separated paths, use .

member.summary: Marks a Module_* class as hidden from the part-authoring "Add Module" picker.

member.name: T:Redux.Modules.Attributes.InlineStringListAttribute
member.summary: Marks a string array or List of string field for inline rendering as a flat list of TextField rows instead of Unity's default foldout-per-element drawer.
member.remarks: Each entry renders as a single-line TextField with a delete button. The list keeps the header-row-with-add-button chrome that the rest of the inline list family uses.

member.name: T:Redux.Modules.Attributes.TransformGroupAttribute
member.summary: Marks a string field whose value is a bare Transform name that the runtime resolves to ALL matching transforms in the part hierarchy via FindModelTransforms / FindChildren.
member.remarks:
Use this when the stored name is expected to group multiple transforms - engine thrust transforms, gimbal targets, linker chain segments, or wheels sharing a transform name. The author-facing widget surfaces the grouping with an autocomplete dropdown of deduplicated names plus a "N matches" chip.
For single-target bare-name references use . For hierarchical-path references resolved via transform.Find(path) use .

member.name: M:Redux.Modules.Module_Mine.GetResumedState(System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Decides which state a mine resumes into once whatever was blocking it has cleared. CheckIngredients auto-disables the mine when an input resource drops below the acceptance threshold, so it stops chattering on and off as the resource crosses that threshold. That can happen while the mine is blocked on containment rather than on resources, so the toggle has to be honoured when resuming from either blocked state instead of only the resource one (#720). Static and free of game state so the mapping can be tested.
member.param: Whether the player currently has the mine toggled on.
Whether the input resources sit above the acceptance threshold.
Whether there is room for at least one of the output resources.
member.returns: The state the mine should resume into.

member.summary: Applies the pending stats delta to both global and campaign stats files. Treats missing or empty files as a fresh rather than throwing. IOExceptions and JSON parse errors are swallowed so a corrupt or partially-written file never aborts callers (e.g. revert-to-VAB) that depend on this completing cleanly.

member.summary: Reads a statistics file, treating one that is missing, empty or unreadable as a fresh .
member.param: Full path to the stats file. A null or empty path counts as missing.
member.returns: The statistics the file holds, or a new when it has none to give.
member.remarks: A stats file left empty by an interrupted write is the case that matters. Reading it with throws "JSON parse error: The document is empty", and the callers that read outside a try block turned that into an exception every frame for the rest of the session.

member.name: T:Redux.Cameras.CameraAnchorBlend
member.summary: Holds the decaying displacement that carries the flight camera anchor from where it sat before a situation change to where the observer sits after it, turning an anchor teleport into a slide.
member.remarks: The displacement is stored in whatever frame the caller recorded the jump in and is never converted here, so this type stays free of the simulation transform hierarchy and can be exercised without a running game.

member.name: F:Redux.Cameras.CameraAnchorBlend.MIN_DURATION
member.summary: The blend duration, in seconds, given to the smallest jump that still slides.

member.name: F:Redux.Cameras.CameraAnchorBlend.MAX_DURATION
member.summary: The longest blend duration, in seconds, that any jump can produce.

member.name: F:Redux.Cameras.CameraAnchorBlend.FULL_DURATION_DISTANCE
member.summary: The jump distance, in meters, at and above which a blend runs for .

member.name: F:Redux.Cameras.CameraAnchorBlend.MIN_JUMP_DISTANCE
member.summary: The smallest jump distance, in meters, that starts a blend.

member.name: F:Redux.Cameras.CameraAnchorBlend.MAX_ADVANCE_STEP
member.summary: The largest amount of blend progress, in seconds, that any single frame may consume.
member.remarks: Docking stalls the main thread for over a hundred milliseconds while view objects are destroyed and physics is unpacked. Advancing by the real elapsed time there spends most of the blend on one frame that never renders an intermediate position, which is seen as a hard cut. The blend is a visual transition, so it advances in rendered frames rather than wall time.

member.summary: The square of , for callers filtering jumps without taking a square root.
