member.name: T:Redux.CelestialBody.ScatterShaderMapping
member.summary: Rebinds Redux stand-in scatter shaders onto their bundled base-game equivalents.
member.remarks: Scatter materials authored in this project cannot reference the base-game scatter shaders directly. Those shaders live in the ksp2.catalog AssetBundle and carry no AssetDatabase GUID, so a serialized reference to one cannot be written into a .mat asset. Materials therefore reference a Redux stand-in declaring the same properties, and the real shader is bound when Vegetation Studio builds its per item material copies. This mirrors what does for the surface material, except that the scatter path has no component of its own to hang the swap on, because the item prefab is never instantiated for the rendered field.

member.name: M:Redux.CelestialBody.ScatterShaderMapping.ResolveBaseGameShaderName(System.String)
member.summary: Maps a Redux stand-in scatter shader name onto its bundled base game equivalent.
member.remarks: Pure name translation, resolved from the string alone, so it is safe to call from anywhere that reasons about shader names rather than shader objects. Shader controller selection needs exactly this: it runs against the name serialized on the material or the vegetation item, which is the stand-in, while the controllers match on the base game name.
member.param: The shader name to translate.
member.returns: The base game name when is a Redux stand-in, otherwise the input unchanged.

member.name: M:Redux.CelestialBody.ScatterShaderMapping.ApplyBaseGameShader(UnityEngine.Material)
member.summary: Rebinds to the bundled scatter shader when it currently uses a Redux stand-in.
member.remarks: Must only ever be handed a material copy. Rebinding a project asset would write the bundled shader reference back into the .mat, which cannot be serialized.
member.param: The material copy to rebind.

member.name: T:Redux.CelestialBody.ReduxSurfaceSpawner
member.summary: Spawns an addressable prefab at a fixed lat/lon/altitude on the parent celestial body, gated by proximity to the active vessel.
member.remarks:
The instance's world pose is recomputed each frame in . The authored lat/lon/altitude and the surface radius sampled once at spawn give a body-local position and rotation in double precision, which the active converts into Unity physics space. That conversion applies the floating-origin offset, so it is the only correct way to reach world space - walking the body transform hierarchy would miss it. All math happens in Vector3d / , and the only precision loss is the final implicit cast to Vector3 near the floating origin where float precision is centimeter-scale.
The addressable handle is released as soon as the prefab is instantiated. The instance is a runtime copy that survives the release. Subsequent spawn cycles re-load the addressable - the trade-off is more I/O on respawn for less memory held while no instance is active.

member.name: T:VSwift.Utilities.SerializedDictionaryEntry`2
member.summary: One key+value record inside a 's Unity-serialized backing list.
member.remarks: Public fields named Key and Value match SerializedArrayTable's column-by-PropertyName lookup convention, so a dictionary can be rendered as a two-column grid without any bespoke scaffold.

member.name: T:VSwift.Utilities.SerializedDictionary`2
member.summary: subclass that round-trips through both Unity's native serializer (via and a backing list of ) and Newtonsoft.Json (via the inherited interface).
member.remarks: Newtonsoft's default contract resolver detects IDictionary on the base type and emits standard {"key": "value"} JSON shape; the private [SerializeField] backing list is skipped because it's private. Unity, conversely, ignores the Dictionary base and only persists the backing list. flushes the dictionary into the list before Unity reads it; rebuilds the dictionary after Unity hydrates it. The backing list carries [JsonIgnore] as an explicit guard against future contract-resolver changes.

member.name: T:SurfaceLandmark
member.summary: Authoring wrapper that coordinates a smoothing decal, prefab spawner, and discoverable entry at one lat/lon on a celestial body.
member.remarks:
Pure data at runtime. The SDK's editor-side sync helper reads these fields and reconciles the three managed children (PQSDecalInstance, ReduxSurfaceSpawner, ScienceRegionData entry) under the PQS. The wrapper GameObject itself is stripped from outgoing scenes by the build pre-process pass. If the strip is skipped for any reason the wrapper is harmless because it has no runtime behavior.
Lat/lon/altitude are the source of truth for placement. The wrapper's Unity transform is a scene-view echo derived from these doubles by the sync helper, not the authoring surface.

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.Latitude
member.summary: Latitude in degrees. North-positive, range [-90, 90].

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.Longitude
member.summary: Longitude in degrees. East-positive, range [-180, 180].

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.Altitude
member.summary: Altitude in meters above the rendered surface height at this lat/lon.

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.SmoothingRadius
member.summary: Smoothing radius in meters. Drives the decal's transform scale (as diameter).

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.SmoothingFadeStrength
member.summary: Fade strength applied to the smoothing decal's edge. Higher values produce a sharper transition between the flat pad and the surrounding terrain. Range mirrors what the runtime shader meaningfully accepts.

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.SmoothingDecal
member.summary: Optional PQSDecal template the smoothing pad sources its appearance from. When null the SDK's default smoothing-pad template is used. Per-instance overrides applied at sync time drive the height behavior regardless of the template choice.

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.DiscoverableRadius
member.summary: Discoverable detection radius in meters. Drives the discoverable entry's radius.

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.EnableDecal
member.summary: Whether the landmark spawns a decal child at all.

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.EnableSmoothing
member.summary: When true, the decal applies smoothing-pad height behavior: replace blend with a height offset of 1 against a flat shared heightmap, scaled by the natural terrain height at the landmark. When false, the decal is purely cosmetic (no terrain modification).

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.EnablePrefab
member.summary: Whether the prefab spawner child is active.

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.EnableDiscoverable
member.summary: Whether the discoverable entry on the body's ScienceRegionData is active.

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.Prefab
member.summary: Prefab the runtime PrefabSpawner spawns. Must be addressable. Ignored when is on.

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.PrefabAddressableKey
member.summary: Raw addressable key used in place of when is on. Lets the artist point at an addressable that isn't available as a typed asset in this project (for example, a base-game key resolved at runtime).

member.name: F:SurfaceLandmark.UseRawAddressableKey
member.summary: Editor-only authoring mode flag. When true, the inspector exposes as a text field instead of the typed slot. The sync helper uses whichever source the toggle selects when writing the spawner's prefab name.

member.summary: Hashes one mod's declared script files plus every other Lua file in its folder into .
member.remarks: The folder sweep is what catches the _-prefixed library files. Those are excluded from a descriptor's declared scripts because they are pulled in with require rather than run as bodies, but they shape patch output all the same, so leaving them out of the key lets an edited library serve stale archives. Sweeping the folder also covers a library required across mods, since every mod's own folder gets swept in turn.
member.param: The mod's folder, or null when it has none.

The patch hash set to record into.

member.name: T:PatchManager.LuaPatching.JsonUserData

member.remarks: Patch scripts read and mutate JSON assets through this type: object keys become string indices, array elements become 1-indexed integer indices (matching Lua convention), and iteration is exposed through the __pairs / __ipairs metamethods on . Reads against the wrong token type are non-fatal. They log a debug message and return or an empty result. Writes against the wrong token type throw, since silently accepting a write would lose data. Subclasses (, ) override these members to layer name-indexed lookup or virtual properties on top of the underlying JSON.

member.summary: JSON-array UserData base class that exposes the array as a name-indexed lookup table.
member.remarks: Subclasses provide an item -> name function via (and optionally a custom item conversion via ), and the base class maintains parallel and caches that translate string keys to array positions and to wrapped item values. Lua scripts then treat the array as if it were a Lua table keyed by item name. String indexing, , and iteration via all operate on names rather than raw JSON object keys. Mutations (, , , ) update the caches in step. String-indexed assignment is intentionally unsupported and always throws. Callers must use the explicit add/remove methods so the name-to-index mapping stays consistent.

member.name: T:PatchManager.LuaPatching.Utility.DelegateRegistry
member.summary: Registers MoonSharp Lua-to-CLR converters for delegate types so Lua functions can be passed directly to CLR APIs that take strongly-typed delegates (, , custom delegate types) of any arity.
member.remarks: MoonSharp only ships built-in conversions for a fixed set of delegate types, so passing a Lua function to a method expecting Action<Foo> would otherwise throw at the boundary. This registry scans a type's methods for delegate parameters via and, for each unique delegate type, compiles a wrapper (via expression trees) that marshals primitives, strings, enums, and UserData both ways. By-ref, out, and pointer parameters are unsupported and the containing delegate type is skipped silently.

member.summary: Wraps an so that string-key lookups that miss the type's declared members fall through to the type's string indexer.

member.name: T:PatchManager.LuaPatching.Universe
member.summary: The central orchestrator for Lua-based patching: loads patch scripts, registers patches and new assets, sorts stages topologically, and runs the resulting pipeline against each patched asset.
member.remarks: Converter and submodule discovery is performed by at module-init time, which populates and by scanning every loaded assembly. Each universe instance then constructs its own and live submodule instances, exposes them as the global PM table, and tracks per-mod patch state. Mods load Lua patches via the LoadPatch* methods, which are expected to register patches and stages through PM. Once loading is done, finalizes ordering and the RunAllPatchesFor overloads execute the chain against each asset.

member.name: M:Uber.Scatter.PqsTerrain.BootForEditor
member.summary: Prepares the GPU sampling resources for editor-mode preview, mirroring the initialization that only happens on the play-mode path.
member.remarks: Both calls are required and in this order. CreateHeightMap, which OnEnable runs outside play mode, populates only the heightmap texture references. CreateComputeShaderResources additionally populates every scale, dimension and contrast the sampling shader reads, so booting without it samples real textures against zeroed scales and returns plausible nonsense instead of failing. Idempotent through the _computeInitDone flag.

member.name: M:Uber.Scatter.PqsTerrain.ShutdownForEditor
member.summary: Releases the GPU sampling resources and clears the initialization flag so a later re-reads PQSData rather than reusing first-boot values.
member.remarks: Deliberately does not repeat the null-PQS guard that OnDisable applies to the same buffers. A preview session can outlive its PQS, and skipping the disposal in that case leaks every persistent allocation this component owns.

member.name: M:Uber.Scatter.PqsTerrain.TextureOrBlack(UnityEngine.Material,System.String)
member.summary: Reads a texture from , substituting black when it is unset.
member.remarks: A body that has not baked every gradience and curvature map leaves the missing ones null, and ComputeShader.SetTexture throws on a null texture rather than ignoring it. Black is the neutral value for all of these maps and matches how CreateComputeShaderResources already falls back for the heightmap stack.
member.param: The surface material to read from.
The texture property to read.
member.returns: The assigned texture, or when unset.

member.name: T:Code.Redux.UI.Flight.WarpToSunriseController
member.summary:
Controller for the "Warp to Next Sunrise" button in the flight HUD time-warp cluster.
The button is always visible. It is interactable when the active vessel is Landed, Splashed, or PreLaunch. While the auto-warp we triggered is running the button shows the Active (green) state. Otherwise it shows the Inactive (orange) state.

member.name: F:Code.Redux.UI.Flight.WarpToSunriseController.DAWN_HOURS
member.summary: Local solar time of dawn, in Earth hours (0-24). Set to 06:00 to land slightly after sunrise.

member.name: F:Code.Redux.UI.Flight.WarpToSunriseController.WARP_BUFFER_DAY_FRACTION
member.summary: Cushion added past the computed dawn time, as a fraction of the body's solar day. Auto-warp deceleration is imprecise and arrives slightly early, so a flat buffer can leave you just shy of dawn and a second click only nudges forward. Scaling with the solar day guarantees arrival solidly past dawn on every body.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_KEEP_ONDISABLE
member.summary: Whether the NGSS directional shadow replacement is kept in Graphics settings when this component is disabled. When false, the custom screen-space shadow shader is removed and the built-in shader is restored on disable.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_NO_UPDATE_ON_PLAY
member.summary: Whether shadow variables are updated only once on scene load rather than every frame during play mode. Enabling this option reduces per-frame CPU overhead.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_SHADOWS_RESOLUTION
member.summary: The shadow map resolution used for directional shadows. defers to the Unity Quality Settings value.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_SAMPLING_TEST
member.summary: The number of samples used for the blocker search and early-bail-out pass. Lower values reduce cost but may introduce white noise. Clamped to [4, 32].

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_SAMPLING_FILTER
member.summary: The number of samples per pixel used by the PCF or PCSS filtering pass. Higher values produce smoother shadows at a greater GPU cost. Clamped to [8, 128].

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_SHADOWS_SOFTNESS
member.summary: The overall softness applied to directional shadows. Clamped to [0, 3].

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_PCSS_ENABLED
member.summary: Whether Percentage Closer Soft Shadows (PCSS) is enabled for area-light-style shadow softness. Requires inline sampling and Shader Model 3.5. When false, uniform PCF filtering is used instead.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_PCSS_SOFTNESS_NEAR
member.summary: The PCSS shadow softness applied to regions close to the shadow caster. Clamped to [0, 2].

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_PCSS_SOFTNESS_FAR
member.summary: The PCSS shadow softness applied to regions far from the shadow caster. Clamped to [0, 2].

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_NOISE_TO_DITHERING_SCALE
member.summary: The blend ratio between noise-based and dithering-based shadow sampling patterns. A value of 0 produces 100% noise. A value of 1 produces 100% dithering.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_NOISE_TEXTURE
member.summary: The noise texture used for shadow sampling patterns when is less than 1. A blue-noise signal texture is recommended.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_DENOISER_ITERATIONS
member.summary: The number of denoiser passes applied to the shadow buffer. Clamped to [1, 3]. Requires the NGSS Shadows Libraries to be installed and Cascaded Shadows enabled in the Editor Graphics Settings.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_DENOISER_BLUR
member.summary: The overall blur radius of the shadow denoiser pass. Clamped to [0, 1].

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_DENOISER_EDGE_TOLERANCE
member.summary: The threshold controlling how much edge detail the denoiser preserves. Clamped to [0.05, 1]. Lower values cause the denoiser to blur across more shadow edges.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_RECEIVER_PLANE_BIAS
member.summary: Whether receiver-plane bias is enabled to tilt the shadow-filtering kernel along the receiver surface slope. Disabled by default because screen-space derivative estimation can produce shadow artifacts.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.GLOBAL_SETTINGS_OVERRIDE
member.summary: Whether this component overrides the global Unity shadow settings (shadow distance, projection, and cascade configuration). When false, those settings are managed through the Unity Quality and Graphics Settings panels.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.GLOBAL_SHADOWS_PROJECTION
member.summary: The shadow projection mode applied globally when is enabled. is recommended to reduce shadow shimmer as the camera moves.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.GLOBAL_SHADOWS_DISTANCE
member.summary: The maximum distance from the camera at which shadows are rendered, in world units. Applied to QualitySettings.shadowDistance when is enabled.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.GLOBAL_CASCADES_COUNT
member.summary: The number of shadow cascade splits. Clamped to [0, 4]. Applied to QualitySettings.shadowCascades when is enabled. Cascaded Shadows should be disabled entirely for low-end target devices.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.GLOBAL_CASCADES_SPLIT_VALUE
member.summary: The base value used to compute exponential cascade split distances in the form x*2^n. Clamped to [0.01, 0.25]. Use 0.1 for four cascades and 0.25 for two cascades. Applied to QualitySettings.shadowCascade4Split and QualitySettings.shadowCascade2Split when is enabled.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_CASCADES_BLENDING
member.summary: Whether cascade seams are blended to hide the transition between adjacent shadow cascades. Enabling this option incurs additional GPU overhead.

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_CASCADES_BLENDING_VALUE
member.summary: The blend distance used for the cascade transition when is enabled. Clamped to [0, 2].

member.name: F:NGSS_Directional.NGSS_CASCADES_SOFTNESS_NORMALIZATION
member.summary: The normalization factor that controls how shadow softness is distributed across cascades. Clamped to [0, 1]. A value of 1 matches softness to the cascade split distribution for realistic distance-based softness. A value of 0 bases softness on cascade index, producing progressively blurrier shadows at distance.

member.name: T:RandomPrefabLoader
member.summary: Randomly selects and asynchronously loads a prefab from a configured list, replacing the active instance each time one reports itself finished.
member.remarks: The main menu's loader does something else entirely: it rotates through published craft, flies them in and out, and turns the planet behind them. That lives in and is built only for the loader that runs in the menu. Every other loader in the game - ten of them dress Mission Control alone - swaps its prefab where it stands, which is what this component did before the menu rotation existed.

member.name: P:RandomPrefabLoader.IsMainMenuVesselLoader
member.summary: Whether this loader is the one the main menu's vessel rotation runs on.
member.remarks: Asked of the loader rather than of the scene. Mission Control's loaders are loaded alongside the menu's own and merely inactive, so anything answered by looking around the scene would call them the menu's too.
